document.title: Your Meeting on Usama bin Laden
document.authors: Assistant Secretary Karl F. Inderfurth to Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, Department of State
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), 1998 Missile Strikes on Bin Laden May Have Backfired
document.note: [Secret] Briefing memorandum outlining key points on bin Laden and how to persuade the Taliban to expel him to a country where he can be brought to justice. The U.S. holds the Taliban responsible, but efforts to get him expelled have been frustrated by his ties to Mullah Omar. Excised.

events.description: Briefing memorandum prepared for the Secretary of State's meeting on how to persuade the Taliban to expel Bin Laden
Assistant Secretary Karl Inderfurth sent a briefing memorandum to the Secretary of State for her meeting on Usama Bin Laden. It sets the goal of persuading the Taliban to expel him from Afghanistan.

relationships.detail: Bin Laden is sheltered in Afghanistan by the Taliban, who are divided over providing him sanctuary; the US holds them responsible for his activities.
relationships.quote: divided on the desirability of providing sanctuary to Bin Laden

relationships.detail: Bin Laden's ties to the Taliban leader are believed to have frustrated efforts to have him expelled. The leader's name is truncated in the text.
relationships.quote: frustrated, we believe, by his ties to Taliban leader Mullah

relationships.detail: The memo says the Taliban have not stopped Afghanistan from being a platform for international terrorism, implying they control it.
relationships.quote: Taliban have not kept Afghanistan from being a platform for international terrorism.

relationships.detail: Bin Laden is in Afghanistan, and the memo discusses the Taliban providing sanctuary to him and being expected to expel him.
relationships.quote: The Taliban themselves are divided on the desirability of providing sanctuary to Bin Laden

relationships.detail: The US holds the Taliban responsible for Bin Laden's activities while he is in Afghanistan.
relationships.quote: responsible for Bin Laden's activities while he is in Afghanistan.

relationships.detail: The memo refers to Bin Laden and his network as continuing to threaten US interests.
relationships.quote: Bin Laden and his network continue to threaten U.S. interests.

relationships.detail: Efforts to get Bin Laden expelled were frustrated, the memo says, by his ties to Taliban leader Mullah Omar (name partly truncated in the OCR).
relationships.quote: frustrated, we believe, by his ties to Taliban leader Mullah

relationships.detail: Mullah Omar is described as the Taliban leader.
relationships.quote: his ties to Taliban leader Mullah

relationships.detail: The US seeks to persuade the Taliban to expel Bin Laden and sees the Taliban's desire for contacts with the US as an incentive.
relationships.quote: To determine how we can persuade the Taliban to expel Usama Bin Laden from Afghanistan

relationships.detail: The US wants Bin Laden expelled and brought to justice because of the threat he poses to US interests.
relationships.quote: he can be brought to justice or otherwise end or limit the threat he poses to U.S. interests

key_claims: The Taliban have not prevented Afghanistan from being a platform for international terrorism.
Bin Laden and his network continue to threaten US interests and personnel.
The US holds the Taliban, and by implication their supporters, responsible for Bin Laden's activities while he is in Afghanistan.
The Taliban are internally divided over giving Bin Laden sanctuary.
Earlier US and Saudi efforts to expel Bin Laden were frustrated, the memo says, by his ties to the Taliban leader.
The Taliban's desire for international contacts, especially with the US, could be an incentive to move on the issue.
